liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Good Lovin'** (3 reviews): Weir's playing stands out during the Good Lovin' jam; Funky jams in Good Lovin' with Jerry ripping leads, at one point recalling Viola Lee [9][14][15]
- **Dark Star** (3 reviews): Dark Star flows into The Other One, with energy intact despite the splice; Dark Star is described as an inventive, unusual version that stretches far from the tune before returning [7][10][15]
- **Turn on Your Lovelight** (3 reviews): The move from Lovelight into Me & My Uncle is praised as excellent, with tight transitions throughout; Pigpen's Lovelight features lively interplay between the band and the crowd [5][7][10]
- **Don't Ease Me In** (2 reviews): Reviewer ranks this among the hottest versions of the song; Don't Ease Me In contains a wild, unexpected jam [5][13]
- **Cold Rain And Snow** (1 review): Jerry's vocal on Cold Rain and Snow is called especially sweet and emotive [11]
- **High Time** (1 review): Jerry's vocal on High Time is called especially sweet and emotive [11]
- **drums** (1 review): The drum solo is well judged and not overlong; Jerry returns and plays a nice duet with the drummers [12]

## The recordings

- **gd70-03-24.sbd.hollister.2990.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 16 songs; 87 min; rated 4.22/5 by 9 [1]. Said about its sound: Vocals on Mama Tried are somewhat low in the recording; The first half of Morning Dew is missing from the circulating tape; A tape flip hits Dark Star at 4:51 before vocals; the remaining fragment resumes after them, losing perhaps 2-4 minutes [1][15]
- **gd70-03-24.sbd.miller.32054.sbeok.flacf**: soundboard; 13 songs; 88 min; rated 4.85/5 by 20 [2]. Said about its sound: Considered an upgrade; a splice at 5:02 in Dark Star doesn't hurt the intensity, and the sound is crisp; Instruments, vocals and audience are well balanced in the mix, with slight hiss; The sound gets sorted out around the second tune, after which the show takes off [7][11][13][14]
- **gd1970-03-24.136667.sbd.sirmick.flac1648**: soundboard; 12 songs; 87 min; rated 2.33/5 by 3 [3]

## Around the show

- The venue's name suggests an amusement park, yet the band rocked hard that night [5]
- A fifteen-year-old attendee came expecting the Chambers Brothers, who had played the previous night, and stayed for the Dead [6]
- Pigpen yelled at the crowd to take their hands out of their pockets [6]
- The show feels like a 1960s-style performance, as many early-1970s shows did [13]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd70-03-24.sbd.hollister.2990.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by David Hollister; source: Soundboard [1]
- **gd70-03-24.sbd.miller.32054.sbeok.flacf**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: Soundboard [2]
- **gd1970-03-24.136667.sbd.sirmick.flac1648**: taped by Anonomous; transferred by SIRMick; source: flac16/48kHz ; Source: Soundboard > Master Reel > Cassette > Dat (48k) [3]

## Art and photos

- Fan art by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead Pirates World - March 24, 1970](https://www.dead.net/show/march-24-1970) [17]
- Poster by lostlivedead.blogspot.com: [March 24, 1970, Pirate's World, Dania, FL (Truckin')](https://lostlivedead.blogspot.com/2015/04/march-24-1970-pirates-world-dania-fl.html) [18]
